title: History of IBM magnetic disk drives
text:
This section lists IBM manufactured HDDs offered both as an OEM product and for attachment to IBMs small systems such as the System/3, System/32, /34 and /36 and the AS/400. HDDs are identified by their OEM model number and listed chronologically by date of first customer shipment.

### IBM 0680

The 0680 first shipped in 1979 on most IBM small systems[1] and the low end of the System/370 as the 3310 direct access storage.[2] The OEM version was announced as the 0680 in September 1981.[3] Developed at IBM's Hursley, UK, laboratory under the code name Piccolo with an initial capacity of up to 65MB, it used six 8-inch disks (210 mm) and had an improved rotary actuator.[4,5]

A double capacity version, the 62SW, shipped in June 1984 but very few units were sold because its price per megabyte was the same as the 62GV.[5]

### IBM 0676

The 0676 first shipped in November 1982 as a 5247 Disk Storage Unit for the IBM System/23 Datamaster.[6] Developed at the IBM Rochester, Minnesota, laboratory as the 21ED it was an 8-inch HDD with an initial capacity of 15 or 30 MB in two or four 210 mm disks. In 1983 it shipped as the HDD in the 5360 System Unit of the S/36. In 1984 its capacity was doubled by doubling the number of tracks per surface and it was incorporated into the 5362 System Unit of the System/36.[7]

### IBM 0665

The 0665 first shipped in October 1985 in the system unit for the PC AT (5170).[8] Developed under the code name "Pixie" at IBM Rochester, Minnesota, it was a 51/4-inch HDD with capacities of 20, 30 and 44 MB.

### IBM 0667

The 0667 first shipped in August 1986.[6] Developed at IBM Rochester, Minnesota, under the code name "Grant", it was a 70 MB ESDI full height 51/4-inch HDD with up to four 130 mm disks.[9] It was offered as a feature on certain models of the PC RT (6150, 6151, 6152) and in System/36 Model System Units (5363, 5364).[10]

### IBM 0669

The 0669 first shipped in 1987.[6] Developed at IBM Rochester, Minnesota, under the code name "Grant-Prime", it was a full-height 51/2-inch HDD with a capacity of up to 115 MB on up to four 130 mm disks.[11] It was the HDD internal to the System/36 5363 System Unit and Series 1 4956 System Unit.[11]

### IBM 0671

The 0671 first shipped in 1987.[6] Developed under the code name "Lee" at IBM Rochester, Minnesota, it was an up to 316 MB ESDI full height 51/4-inch HDD with up to eight 130 mm disks depending upon model.[11] This was IBM's first usage of a thin metal film as the disk's recording surface.[11] In 1988 it shipped as part of the 9404 System Unit of the IBM AS/400 system which contained two, or optionally three of these HDDs.[12]

### IBM 0661

The 0661 first shipped in 1989 as the model 371.[13] Developed initially under the code name "Lightning" at IBM Rochester Minnesota (and IBM Hursley, UK) as a 320 MB SCSI HDD with up to eight 95 mm disks (14 heads), it was followed in 1990 with a 400 MB version, code named "Turbo". During 1990 it was added as a standard drive on several major IBM systems,[13] e.g., IBM AS/400 System Unit Model CXX.[14]

### IBM 0681

The 0681 first shipped in April 1990. Developed at IBM's Hursley, UK, laboratory under the code name Redwing, it was the last HDD product developed at Hursley.[15] It was an up to 857 MB full-height 51/4-inch HDD using up to 12 130 mm disks. It was the first HDD to use PRML decoding of data.[16] It was the drive component of the 9333 Disk Drive Subsystem which first shipped in early 1992.

A higher density, 1.07 GB, version was incorporated into the 9333 subsystem in May 1992.[17]

### IBM 0663

The 0663 first shipped in late 1991. Developed under the code name "Corsair", it was a 31/2-inch HDD with the height of a 51/2-inch half-height device (1.6-inch high) and up to 1 GB on up to 8 95 mm disks.[18,19] It was offered as a feature on certain models of the PS/2 and RS/6000.[19] It was the first OEM disk drive to use MR Heads.[16]

### IBM 0664

The 0664 first shipped in November 1992. Developed under the code name "Allicat" at IBM Rochester, Minnesota, it was a full-height 51/2-inch HDD (3.25-inch high) that combined two 31/2-inch devices in one, with up to 2.013 GB capacity on up to 8 95 mm disks.[20,21]

### IBM 0662

The 0662 first shipped in June 1993. Developed under the code name "Spitfire" at IBM Rochester, Minnesota, it was a full-height (1-inch high) 31/2-inch HDD with 1.05 GB on three disks or five disk surfaces.[21,22,23] It was the HDD internal to the 9336 Disk Unit and the 9337 Disk Array.[21]
